stories.headline: SC Issues Notice to Centre, ECI on Plea Challenging Blanket Immunity for Election Commissioners
stories.title: SC Issues Notice to Centre, ECI on Plea Challenging Blanket Immunity for Election Commissioners
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Tuesday issued notice to the Centre and the Election Commission of India (ECI) on a public interest litigation challenging the blanket immunity granted to the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and other Election Commissioners under Section 16 of the Chief Election Commissioner and the other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023.

A bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana sought responses from the Union government and the poll panel on a plea filed by the Association for Democratic Reforms (ADR) challenging the provision that grants serving and former CECs and Election Commissioners immunity from legal proceedings for acts, things or words committed, done or spoken in the course of discharging, or purporting to discharge, their official duties.
As per the case status available on the apex court’s website, the matter is tentatively listed for further hearing on November 2.

Section 16 states: "Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, no Court shall entertain or continue any civil or criminal proceedings against any person who is or was a Chief Election Commissioner or an Election Commissioner for any act, thing or word, committed, done or spoken by him when, or in the course of acting or purporting to act in the discharge of his official duty or function."

ADR has contended that the provision violates Articles 14 and 19 of the Constitution, arguing that granting such sweeping protection to the constitutional functionaries undermines accountability and places them beyond the ordinary process of law.

The plea has questioned the grant of blanket immunity to the CEC and Election Commissioners, contending that the provision could shield alleged arbitrary exercise of power and corruption from judicial scrutiny.

stories.headline: Technology, innovation must benefit all: PM Modi
stories.title: Technology, innovation must benefit all: PM Modi
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 13: Prime Minister NarendraModi on Tuesday called for using technology, data, knowledge, and innovation to empower people rather than concentrate power in the hands of a few, saying India's growth should create opportunities for the world. Addressing the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi, being held in India for the first time, PM Modi said the real question was not who possessed power but how it was used. “Today, Technology is Power, Data is Power, Knowledge is Power, Innovation is Power,” he said. “But friends, the real question is not who possesses power. Rather, the question is how that power is being used.” Emphasising his vision of inclusive growth, the PM said: “Beyond Power to Control lies Power to Enable. Beyond Power to Compete lies Power to Collaborate. Beyond Power to Succeed lies Power to Help Others Succeed. And therefore, the vision with which I have come here today is: Power to Empower.” He said India had sought to put this philosophy into practice through digital connectivity, affordable mobile data, digital payments and innovation. PM Modi said that these initiatives had expanded access to opportunities for students, small traders and young people, including those in smaller towns and villages. “Connectivity in India has not merely connected people; it has connected opportunities as well. This, indeed, is Power to Empower,” he said. Highlighting India's startup ecosystem, the PM said the country had more than 2.50 lakh startups, compared with only a few hundred before 2014. He said nearly half of these startups came from small cities and towns, while more than 45 percent had at least one woman director or partner. PM Modi also underlined the role of technology in governance, citing the JAM Trinity and Direct Benefit Transfer system, which enables government assistance to reach beneficiaries directly through their bank accounts. “The government possesses authority, but its purpose should not be to make citizens dependent on the system. Rather, its objective should be to ensure that citizens become capable and empowered,” he said. The PM said that India had lifted 25 crore people out of poverty over the past decade. India's role in a changing world He said the world was facing growing uncertainty due to wars, disruptions in trade, shortages of critical minerals and energy supplies, and rapid technological change. “Supply chains, energy, minerals, payment systems, and technology are increasingly becoming instruments of pressure and dominance,” PM Modi said, warning that routes created by globalisation had, in many cases, become chokepoints. In such circumstances, he said, trust had become a fundamental requirement, including confidence that supplies would continue during a crisis and partner countries would stand by one another. “We do not grow at anyone's cost. We grow with the world, and for the world,” the PM said. He cited India's contribution to global healthcare, digital public infrastructure, and skilled manpower, noting that one in every five generic medicines used worldwide came from India and that the country hosted more than 2,000 Global Capability Centres serving companies across the world. PM Modi also said India shared its digital capabilities with other countries, particularly those in the Global South. During the COVID-19 pandemic, India supplied vaccines to more than 100 countries, he said. On climate change, the PM said India had achieved its target of sourcing 40 percent of installed electricity capacity from non-fossil fuel sources in November 2021, nine years ahead of its 2030 deadline under the Paris Agreement. He said India's renewable energy capacity had risen from around 75 gigawatts in 2014 to approximately 300 gigawatts. Referring to the PM Surya Ghar and PM-KUSUM schemes, PM Modi said they were helping households and farmers generate solar power, reduce costs, and contribute to lower carbon emissions. He also highlighted India's economic performance, stating that the economy had grown by 7.8 percent in the April-June quarter. The PM said foreign exchange reserves exceeded USD 700 billion, while the current account deficit had fallen to 0.61 percent of GDP in the previous year. Listing reforms undertaken by the government, he referred to the Goods and Services Tax (GST), the Insolvency and Bankruptcy framework, the consolidation of 29 labour laws into four labour codes and the decriminalisation of hundreds of minor business-related offences. “For us, reforms are not a compulsion. Reforms are our conviction,” PM Modi said. He called for greater international cooperation to address challenges like climate change, water governance, public health, and the responsible use of emerging technologies. “Power is not just the ability to move ahead. It is also the ability to empower others to move ahead,” the PM said, adding that competition was important but compassion was equally necessary and the benefits of innovation should be widely shared.

stories.headline: Can RBI’s six forex measures help stabilise the rupee?
stories.title: Can RBI’s six forex measures help stabilise the rupee?
stories.summary: Kolkata: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has taken a slew of steps since Saturday to help lift the rupee to what Governor Sanjay Malhotra described as its "correct" value. These measures have helped the rupee recover to 95.28 a dollar, about 150 paise over two days. An immediate fallout is the reduction in speculative bets on the currency and discouraging over-hedging by companies in anticipation of further rupee depreciation. An inevitable inflation in hedging costs, a natural outcome of the reserves to be set aside by banks against client exposures, has caused some noses to wrinkle in the importer community.Separately, total removal of the dollar needs of three state-run fuel retailers from the spot rupee market reduces the pressure on the currency.Here's an ET explainer on the measures taken by the central bank and their impact.Introduction of Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve (FERR)A first-time measure imposing a 20% cash reserve requirement on large forex derivatives contracts over $2 million. This means banks will have to set aside funds as a percentage of their total exposure, and that money will no longer be available for onlending until the exposure is fully cancelled.For instance, for a $10 million hedging contract for a client, a bank will have to keep around ₹19 crore everyday with the central bank until the expiry of the contract. This money is not available for lending.Hence, banks will have to pass on this cost to their clients. This would inflate the hedging cost for importers by at least 150 basis points (one basis point is a hundredth of a percentage point) and, therefore, they would be discouraged to hedge their exposure, experts said.Read more: Anand Rathi Share and Stock Brokers Q2 results: Profit jumps 50% YoY to Rs 42 crore, revenue rises 20%FERR Impact on the Forwards MarketsAnother fallout of the FERR curbs is an immediate cut in the rates on forward premium, as the aggregate demand for hedging itself would reduce. Since importers would keep open positions, it would ultimately soften forward premium rates, currency experts believe. Softening forward premiums will also help reduce pressure on the spot rupee in the local market.However, a section of the importers is worried their cost would climb significantly as the funds needed to hedge will eat into their working capital buffers, potentially requiring them to borrow to plug the gap.Read more: Strong buzz! Reliance Jio said to see over $20 billion bids as investors line up for India's biggest IPOExtension of FERR restrictions for contracts with overseas entitiesThe regulator Monday widened the ambit of FERR, extending the rule for non-deliverable contracts involving rupee to non-resident customers, only for the purpose of hedging. The move also eliminates the probability of dollar hoarding by companies and importers because of the steep FERR costs, limiting their dollar exposure to genuine and foreseeable business needs.Threshold for foreign exchange derivative transactions reducedThe limit has been reduced to $5 million equivalent from $100 million across all authorised dealers. This will curb speculative trading in the rupee. A corresponding reduction has been introduced in exchange-traded currency derivatives involving the rupee, across stock exchanges taken together.Restrictions on rebooking of cancelled foreign exchange derivative contractsBanks cannot allow users to rebook any previously cancelled foreign exchange derivative contract involving the rupee - whether deliverable or non-deliverable. Rollover of foreign exchange derivative contracts on maturity shall continue to be permitted.Special dollar window for State-run oil retailersThe RBI would use its own dollar stockpile to meet the daily dollar needs of Indian Oil Corp, Bharat Petroleum Corp and Hindustan Petroleum Corp. This reduces dollar demand in the spot market, easing the pressure on rupee.This would also mask the underlying pressure on balance of payments while dollars will be drained from the central bank's foreign exchange reservess. The Reserve Bank of India opened this window Monday, albeit for a temporary period.Stricter verificationRBI tells banks to obtain additional documentation for verification of underlying exposures. This will prevent users from entering into foreign exchange derivative contracts involving the rupee to hedge contracted exposures, using the same underlying exposure that has been hedged with any other bank. Banks have to keep the documents for a minimum two-year period.Overall views of forex market and treasury professionalsEconomists see these measures as tactical steps to support the rupee, not structural solutions ensuring its durable stability. They believe that defending the rupee amid the continued geopolitical headwinds would be a costly policy trade-off, requiring broader capital market reforms to encourage stable and long term foreign capital inflows.India still levies a security transactions tax, even when the long-term capital gains tax was reintroduced in 2018, and increased it to 12.5% last year. Experts suggest a broader response spanning lowering of taxes, exchange-rate flexibility and further monetary policy tightening to bolster the rupee.

opening: Kolkata: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has taken a slew of steps since Saturday to help lift the rupee to what Governor Sanjay Malhotra described as its "correct" value.
These measures have helped the rupee recover to 95.28 a dollar, about 150 paise over two days.
body: An immediate fallout is the reduction in speculative bets on the currency and discouraging over-hedging by companies in anticipation of further rupee depreciation.
An inevitable inflation in hedging costs, a natural outcome of the reserves to be set aside by banks against client exposures, has caused some noses to wrinkle in the importer community.
Separately, total removal of the dollar needs of three state-run fuel retailers from the spot rupee market reduces the pressure on the currency.
Here's an ET explainer on the measures taken by the central bank and their impact.
Introduction of Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve (FERR)A first-time measure imposing a 20% cash reserve requirement on large forex derivatives contracts over $2 million.
This means banks will have to set aside funds as a percentage of their total exposure, and that money will no longer be available for onlending until the exposure is fully cancelled.
For instance, for a $10 million hedging contract for a client, a bank will have to keep around ₹19 crore everyday with the central bank until the expiry of the contract.
This money is not available for lending.
Hence, banks will have to pass on this cost to their clients.

This would inflate the hedging cost for importers by at least 150 basis points (one basis point is a hundredth of a percentage point) and, therefore, they would be discouraged to hedge their exposure, experts said.

Anand Rathi Share and Stock Brokers Q2 results: Profit jumps 50% YoY to Rs 42 crore, revenue rises 20%FERR Impact on the Forwards MarketsAnother fallout of the FERR curbs is an immediate cut in the rates on forward premium, as the aggregate demand for hedging itself would reduce.
Since importers would keep open positions, it would ultimately soften forward premium rates, currency experts believe.
Softening forward premiums will also help reduce pressure on the spot rupee in the local market.

However, a section of the importers is worried their cost would climb significantly as the funds needed to hedge will eat into their working capital buffers, potentially requiring them to borrow to plug the gap.
Strong buzz!
Reliance Jio said to see over $20 billion bids as investors line up for India's biggest IPOExtension of FERR restrictions for contracts with overseas entities.
The regulator Monday widened the ambit of FERR, extending the rule for non-deliverable contracts involving rupee to non-resident customers, only for the purpose of hedging.
The move also eliminates the probability of dollar hoarding by companies and importers because of the steep FERR costs, limiting their dollar exposure to genuine and foreseeable business needs.
Threshold for foreign exchange derivative transactions reduced.
The limit has been reduced to $5 million equivalent from $100 million across all authorised dealers.
This will curb speculative trading in the rupee.
A corresponding reduction has been introduced in exchange-traded currency derivatives involving the rupee, across stock exchanges taken together.

Restrictions on rebooking of cancelled foreign exchange derivative contractsBanks cannot allow users to rebook any previously cancelled foreign exchange derivative contract involving the rupee - whether deliverable or non-deliverable.
Rollover of foreign exchange derivative contracts on maturity shall continue to be permitted.
Special dollar window for State-run oil retailers.
The RBI would use its own dollar stockpile to meet the daily dollar needs of Indian Oil Corp, Bharat Petroleum Corp and Hindustan Petroleum Corp.
This reduces dollar demand in the spot market, easing the pressure on rupee.
This would also mask the underlying pressure on balance of payments while dollars will be drained from the central bank's foreign exchange reservess.
The Reserve Bank of India opened this window Monday, albeit for a temporary period.
Stricter verificationRBI tells banks to obtain additional documentation for verification of underlying exposures.

This will prevent users from entering into foreign exchange derivative contracts involving the rupee to hedge contracted exposures, using the same underlying exposure that has been hedged with any other bank.
Banks have to keep the documents for a minimum two-year period.
Overall views of forex market and treasury professionalsEconomists see these measures as tactical steps to support the rupee, not structural solutions ensuring its durable stability.

They believe that defending the rupee amid the continued geopolitical headwinds would be a costly policy trade-off, requiring broader capital market reforms to encourage stable and long term foreign capital inflows.
India still levies a security transactions tax, even when the long-term capital gains tax was reintroduced in 2018, and increased it to 12.5% last year.
Experts suggest a broader response spanning lowering of taxes, exchange-rate flexibility and further monetary policy tightening to bolster the rupee.

stories.title: Legal Immunity For CEC, ECs: Supreme Court notice to Centre, ECI
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has issued notice to the Centre and Election Commission on an ADR petition challenging Section 16 of the 2023 law that grants immunity to the CEC and ECs from civil and criminal proceedings.

corroboration: 2 independent source groups -> high confidence

article_sentences: The plea seeks revival of proceedings against current and past CEC/Election Commissioners.

The Supreme Court today issued notice on a petition filed by the Association for Democratic Reforms challenging the immunity granted to Chief Election Commissioner/Election Commissioners for actions taken in purported discharge of official duties.

A bench of CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana sought the response of the Union and the Election Commission on ADR's challenge to the constitutional validity of Section 16 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023.
Senior Advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan appeared for ADR.
The petition has been filed through AoR Rani Mishra.
Briefly put, the petition seeks a declaration that Section 16 of the CEC Act is unconstitutional, void and inoperative as violative of Articles 14 and 21 and the basic structure of the Constitution.
It further seeks revival of proceedings against the present and past CEC and Election Commissioners, which came to an end as Section 16 of the CEC Act came into effect.

"Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, no Court shall entertain or continue any civil or criminal proceedings against any person who is or was a Chief Election Commissioner or an Election Commissioner for any act, thing or word, committed, done or spoken by him when, or in the course of acting or purporting to act in the discharge of his official duty or function."
The petition contends that Section 16 provides blanket immunity to the current and previous CEC/ECs for lifetime, which has no rational nexus with the objective of ensuring independence of CEC/ECs.
The provision places the CEC & ECs beyond the reach of any Court of law, it highlights.
"No other provision in the Constitution of India or any statute grants immunity that is at once lifelong, unconditioned by good faith, free of any sanction mechanism, and without a saving clause."
Petitioner-ADR further points out that Section 16 was not originally part of the Bill introduced.

stories.title: Response to petitions on illegal detention, clampdown is ready, but needs fine-tuning: Centre
stories.summary: A three-judge Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant extended the time for the government to file the reply affidavit by October 15, 2026
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence

article_sentences: The Union government informed the Supreme Court on Tuesday (October 13, 2026) that its response to petitions alleging illegal detentions, shutdown of public and rail transport, including Metro service, in Delhi on October 10 is “ready” but needs more fine-tuning.
A three-judge Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant extended the time for the government to file the reply affidavit by October 15.
Multiple petitions, including ones seeking contempt proceedings, were adjourned to October 15, 2026 as one of the judges on the Bench was unwell.
The Bench rose for the day shortly thereafter.
Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, for the Centre, said he had gone through the prepared affidavit.
It was final, but he wanted to make it “more comprehensive”.

On the petitioners’ request, the Court asked him to share the affidavit, if possible, by October 14, 2026, a day before the hearing so that the lawyers of the petitioners were suitably well-versed with the contents of the affidavit and the hearing would be a meaningful one.

The Court also agreed to urgently hear fresh petitions seeking independent probe and contempt proceedings against authorities on the continued police action against journalists, especially women media professionals, covering the anti-CEC/SIR protests despite an apex court order against it on October 11.
Chief Justice Kant asked the petitioners to cure defects, after which the pleas would also be put up for a comprehensive hearing on Thursday (October 15, 2026).
The Court asked for a senior police officer to be present during the next hearing, when allegations of assault on women are raised in the courtroom.

Members of the Supreme Court Bar Association and Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association, of which petitions were adjourned on October 13, gathered at the Supreme Court lawns to express solidarity with the advocates who were assaulted and detained by the police during the October 10 and 11 protests.
A separate petition was orally mentioned by senior advocate Gaurav Bhatia about the “sad” incident which happened in the Supreme Court on October 12, 2026.

stories.headline: GK correspondent among 24 journalists complete DCC 2026
stories.title: GK correspondent among 24 journalists complete DCC 2026
stories.summary: Jammu, Oct 13: Greater Kashmir correspondent Sumit Bhargav is among 24 journalists from across the country, who have successfully completed the Defence Correspondents Course (DCC 2026), conducted by the Ministry of Defence, Government of India, under its Directorate of Public Relations from September 21 to October 10. The Defence Correspondents Course concluded at Tezpur. Its Navy leg was conducted at Vizag (Visakhapatnam), followed by the Air Force leg at Tezpur and the Indian Army leg at Tezpur, Tenga and Tawang. “The three-weeks course provided participating journalists with an understanding of the roles, capabilities and operational environments of the three Services,” the Ministry of Defence said. The valedictory function was chaired by Lieutenant General Neeraj Shukla, General Officer Commanding, Gajraj Corps. Vijay Kumar, Additional Director General (Media and Communication), Ministry of Defence, along with officials of the Directorate of Public Relations, also attended the event. The course is conducted annually by the Ministry of Defence, Government of India through the Directorate of Public Relations. After receiving applications from journalists from across the country, a strict screening-criteria is followed that includes in-depth analysis of professional working, experience and reporting intellect of aspirants followed by an interaction which is conducted by a team of officers of concerned authority. Greater Kashmir correspondent Sumit Bhargav was selected for DCC 2026 after he successfully fulfilled all the prerequisites of the Ministry of Defence. The course started on September 21 from Vizag (Visakhapatnam) where its Navy leg was conducted wherein twenty four journalists from across the country attended the proceedings at Eastern Naval Command. Beside going through presentations and allied aspects, the journalists also got a rare opportunity to see submariners beside taking a sea sortie in a Destroyer ship wherein they (journalists) understood the circumstances in which Navy personnel carry out their professional assignments despite multiple challenges that primarily include difficult sea states. Navy Leg was followed by Indian Air Force leg that was held at Air Force Station Tezpur wherein beside all other important aspects of studying the working of Air Force, the Journalists got a thrilling opportunity to witness a real time mock drill of response of pilots towards an emergency situation from adversaries beside a night time sortie of SU-30 MKI fighter plane. Under the umbrella of 4 Corps of Indian Army, referred to as Gajraj Corps under Eastern Army Command, the Army leg of DCC 2026 was conducted in areas of Arunachal Pradesh focussing on Indo-China LAC. The Army keg started from Gajraj Corps HQ after which journalists were taken to Tenga where they not only studied the working mode of army troops on LAC but also joined army troops in their day to day working schedule that especially included firing practices. The journalists on DCC 2026 were taken to Tawang which is a high-altitude area in Arunachal Pradesh and is strategically very important as it is located on Indo-China LAC. At Tawang, the journalists visited a number of strategic LAC locations including Bumla LAC point where cross border meetings are held while army personnel of both Indian and Chinese armies standing next to each other followed by visits to holy waterfall, holy tree, Border Brew cafe and other LAC locations. The Journalists got a rare opportunity to understand the situation on LAC and the way troops of the Indian Army are guarding LAC despite tough weather conditions and other multiple challenges. At the high altitude area of Tawang, Journalists also joined army troops in night patrolling and alongside a Bada Khana (social evening) to spend time with troops together. Defence Correspondents Course 2026 concluded at Corps Headquarters Tezpur wherein General Officer Commanding (GOC), Gajraj Corps ( 4 Corps ), Lt Gen Neeraj Shukla interacted with DCC Journalists and both sides shared experiences with each other on a range of issues. The Journalists also shared their experiences of entire DCC proceedings that especially included visits to forward LAC locations. During this event, Lt Gen Neeraj Shukla felicitated Greater Kashmir Correspondent Sumit Bhargav who has successfully completed Defence Correspondents Course and has been empanelled with Ministry of Defence as a Defence Journalist. Through a series of briefings, field visits and interactions with military personnel, the participants gained insights into the functioning of the defence forces and the responsibilities associated with defence reporting, a statement of the Ministry of Defence read. The engagement also strengthened mutual understanding between the defence forces and the media, underscoring their shared commitment to enhancing public awareness while maintaining due regard for operational sensitivities and national security considerations, the Ministry further stated. Sharing his perspective, Sumit Bhargav said, “Defence Correspondents Course is a vital step by MoD's Directorate of Public Relations which is mainly aimed to ensure that both reporting on defence aspects of country and national security do not clash with each other.” He stated, “Many a time, Fastest Fingers First and Breaking News syndrome on issues related to the defence sector prove detrimental to national security and can even prove handy for adversaries for which journalists also need to maintain a constructive approach.” He further said that during DCC, all the journalists attending the course came to know about the country's fast progress in the defence sector and steps being taken to strengthen the security and defence apparatus especially under Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative.

stories.headline: Rahul Gandhi hints at next move in CEC-SIR row, says protests will continue
stories.title: Rahul Gandhi hints at next move in CEC-SIR row, says protests will continue
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 13: Congress leader & Leader of Opposition, Rahul Gandhi on Tuesday indicated that the INDIA bloc would continue its campaign against the government over the functioning of the Election Commission (EC), but declined to disclose the opposition’s next move, saying he did not want to “spoil the surprise”. According to The Times of India, Gandhi made the remarks while addressing reporters at a joint briefing of opposition parties at his residence, where he hosted leaders for evening tea. He said the protests would continue until the opposition achieved its objective. “Sooner or later, whether tomorrow, the day after, in three months, six months, a year, or two years, it (protests) will not stop. It will reach the end goal. I cannot tell you exactly how we will get there, because that would spoil the surprise, and we want to maintain the excitement and sense of surprise for you and the country,” Rahul Gandhi said. The Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha asserted that the Congress-led INDIA bloc would sustain its campaign with the same energy, strength and unity with which it had mobilised against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Gandhi also expressed respect for the Supreme Court and Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, while making it clear that the opposition would continue its political campaign irrespective of the outcome of judicial proceedings. “Thank you to the Supreme Court—we have immense respect for the Supreme Court, the Chief Justice of India, and the Indian judicial system. They have a role to play, and we hope they will play it. However, we are political people; no matter what happens, or which institution plays a role or doesn’t, political resistance will continue, people’s resistance will continue, and it will triumph,” he said. Rahul Gandhi’s remarks came a day after he and 10 other opposition leaders approached the Supreme Court in the matter. The petition names the Election Commission, CEC Gyanesh Kumar and Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi as respondents. Gyanesh Kumar, who became Chief Election Commissioner in 2025 after serving on the Election Commission, has repeatedly faced allegations from opposition parties of favouring the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). The allegations have been contested amid the wider political debate over the functioning and impartiality of the poll body. The latest developments have brought the Election Commission’s decision-making process and the SIR exercise under renewed political and judicial scrutiny, with the opposition signalling that its campaign will continue alongside the proceedings in the Supreme Court.

stories.headline: In meeting with Rubio, Jaishankar raises India’s concerns about sanctions Act
stories.title: In meeting with Rubio, Jaishankar raises India’s concerns about sanctions Act
stories.summary: The External Affairs Minister and the Secretary of State are also understood to be preparing for high-level meetings between U.S. President Donald Trump and Prime Minister Narendra Modi later this year
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: In their first meeting since the United States enacted the Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act (SRIA), External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar raised concerns about the law with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio in New York on Wednesday (September 23, 2026).

The law, which mandates U.S. President Donald Trump to penalise countries that buy Russian oil with up to 100% tariffs, and extends sanctions on Iran trade, could affect India if implemented after the stipulated one-month period.
In a social media post, Mr. Jaishankar said he had “reiterated India’s interests and concerns with regard to SRIA” and discussed the situations in Ukraine and Iran.

In a strongly worded reaction to the U.S. Congress passing the Act last week, the Ministry of External Affairs had said it conveyed to various U.S. interlocutors in recent months that the move would have “implications” for both the India-U.S. bilateral relationship and the international energy market if India is pressured by the U.S. to drop its intake of Russian Ural, which currently makes up 51% of India’s total crude oil imports.
After the meeting, Mr. Rubio sidestepped the issue.

In a social media post about the meeting with Mr. Jaishankar, he said, “Together, we are building on the U.S.-India strategic partnership and coordinating on key regional priorities and upcoming multilateral efforts.”

Mr. Jaishankar and Mr. Rubio are also understood to be preparing for high-level meetings between U.S. President Donald Trump and Prime Minister Narendra Modi later this year, with a possible meeting at the ASEAN Summit in November and then a bilateral meeting expected in mid-December, when Mr. Trump hosts the G20 Summit in Miami.

This is the third year in succession that India has failed to host the Quad Summit, and New Delhi has been keen to set a date later this year or in the first part of 2027 for Mr. Trump and leaders of Australia and Japan to travel to India.
There has not been a breakthrough on a date thus far.

The External Affairs Minister and the Secretary of State have met often and extremely cordially in the past two years, even as bilateral relations have come under strain over U.S. tariffs on India, the Free Trade Agreement negotiations, and the U.S.’s ties with Pakistan in the aftermath of Operation Sindoor last year.
Their meeting on Wednesday came on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA), which Mr. Trump addressed a day earlier.
In his address on Tuesday, Mr. Trump repeated a claim, which has been denied on several occasions by the Modi government, that he negotiated the India-Pakistan ceasefire in May 2025.

stories.headline: Jitendra Singh backs science-led solutions for Himalayan challenges at SKUAST-K summit
stories.title: Jitendra Singh backs science-led solutions for Himalayan challenges at SKUAST-K summit
stories.summary: Srinagar, Oct 13: Union Minister for Science and Technology and Earth Sciences, Dr. Jitendra Singh, on Tuesday expressed support for translating scientific research into practical, scalable solutions for the Himalayan region on the second day of the J&K Agriculture Science Congress and the 13th Sustainable Mountain Development Summit (SMDS) 2026 at Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology of Kashmir (SKUAST-K), Shalimar. Emphasising the need for outcomes beyond deliberations, Dr. Singh highlighted government programmes focused on the Himalayas and initiatives monitoring climate change, including glacier dynamics and glacial lake outburst floods (GLOFs). He welcomed SKUAST-K’s collaboration with the Integrated Mountain Initiative (IMI) and other institutions in preparing a draft Sustainable Mountain Development Policy for Jammu and Kashmir. He noted that stakeholder consultations could further strengthen the framework and indicated that the proposal could be considered by the Government of India. SKUAST-K Vice-Chancellor Prof. Nazir Ahmad Ganai highlighted the university’s role in addressing regional challenges through research and innovation. He said the university had secured 146 patents and nurtured 115 startups. He added that the summit aimed to identify practical approaches to safeguarding mountain ecosystems and communities. Arushi Chopra, Director at SYSTEMIQ, stressed the need for a Himalayan Mountain Development Policy that balances ecological conservation with economic priorities, highlighting the role of sustainable infrastructure. Dr. S. K. Panigrahi, Director General of IISD India, noted that Himalayan catchment systems support nearly 40 per cent of India’s population, underscoring the wider consequences of disasters in the region. In his welcome address, Dr. Rajan Kotru of IMI stressed the importance of institutional conviction, collaboration and commitment in addressing Himalayan challenges. He called for closer integration of policy, practice and scientific knowledge to ensure that the summit’s outcomes are widely supported and translated into policy action. Sushil Ramola, former President of IMI, emphasised the need to convert scientific knowledge into inclusive policies and strengthen the link between research and decision-making. Babila Rakhwal, Commissioner Secretary, Department of Science and Technology, Government of Jammu and Kashmir, reaffirmed the department’s commitment to science- and technology-based initiatives for sustainable mountain development. The proceedings concluded with a vote of thanks by Prof. A. H. Mughal, Dean, Faculty of Forestry, SKUAST-K.
